subject: Right-sized license & support bundle for on-prem pilot
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clariohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@clariohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private install — pilot scope and cost anchors

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Rahul and I chatted internally — we like Redwood's runtime and the KV caching story, but procurement asked for a clear, small-scale on-prem pilot price we can take to our finance team. Two asks from our side: 1) a short-term (3 month) pilot license we can treat as Opex with a simple per-GPU seat number, and 2) an optional short SLA add-on (24x5) that we can toggle on if we validate production traffic.

Separately, security wants to understand if the platform fee can be deferred until after pilot acceptance or if you can offer a pro-rated credit applied to the platform fee when we convert to a full license.

Could you sketch a conservative commercial for a 2x A40 on-prem pilot + 1 SRE retainer? We mostly need the numbers to show to procurement this week.

Best,
Priya Shah
Director of ML Platforms, Clario Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clariohealth.com>
Cc: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@clariohealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private install — pilot scope and cost anchors

Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can do a compact pilot construct that keeps the platform fee from being a near-term blocker. High-level sketch below (I attached a short PDF and MAAP worksheet):

- Pilot term: 3 months, 2x A40 equivalent nodes
- License: temporary pilot subscription, flat $18,000/month (includes runtime license + minor on-prem packaging)
- Platform fee: $6,000/month (normally billed up-front) — we can either defer billing until conversion or bill month-to-month and credit entire pilot platform fee against the first 6 months if you convert within 90 days
- SRE retainer: $4,000/month (on-call 24x5 response; 8 hours/week allocation)
- One-time onboarding: $9,000 (includes on-prem install checklist, security hardening runbook) — can be amortized into conversion credit at 50% if you move to an annual contract

We'd expect a standard conversion path: 12–24 month committed license with an amortized platform fee (we typically propose spreading platform fee over first 12 months). I'll loop in Laura (contracts) and Marissa (commercial structuring) to confirm legal and credit mechanics.

If that direction works, I can produce a concise SOW + commercial term sheet today for procurement.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clariohealth.com>, Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@clariohealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private install — pilot scope and cost anchors

Jordan / Marissa — quick note on the platform fee crediting approach. Two safe concession patterns that limit accounting exposure while giving the customer the commercial comfort they want:

1) Deferred billing + conversion credit: bill the platform fee month-to-month during the pilot, but include an explicit conversion credit in the term sheet that redeems paid pilot platform fee against the first N months (N = min(6, conversion_term_months)). This avoids cash flow surprises for us while being simple for procurement.

2) Up-front deferral with conditional credit memo: we defer invoicing for the platform fee during the pilot and issue a conditional credit memo on conversion. This is cleaner for the customer but requires Finance sign-off on revenue recognition timing.

Also propose the following guardrails on the SRE retainer: capped-hour model (8 hrs/week, up to 32 hrs/month) and a one-time migration assist at onboarding. If Clario wants deeper SLA (24x7 or stronger RTOs) that moves into a premium support tier priced separately.

Marissa — can you confirm what margin / discount band we can give on onboarding if we commit the onboarding as credit at conversion? Also flag any standard DocuSign clause we should add for pilot-to-production conversion (auto-roll into annual unless terminated within 30 days of pilot end).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@clariohealth.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clariohealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private install — pilot scope and cost anchors

Jordan / Laura / Marissa — this looks reasonable and actionable. A few procurement-legal notes from our side: 1) we prefer the deferred billing + conversion credit pattern (option 1) — easier for our accounting; 2) onboarding cost treatment: ideally show onboarding as a separately invoiced item that is 50% refundable as a credit on conversion; 3) can you add a short clause that defines "pilot acceptance" (basic smoke test + security checklist signoff) so we have objective conversion criteria.

We're ready to take the SOW to procurement once you send a 1-page commercial summary and the short SOW. Can you email the doc and a DocuSign link?

Thanks — Rahul
VP, Infrastructure Engineering | Clario Health
